messages.content:
You fill a fixed schema from one page of a technical document about machines at work: a manufacturer's
manual (robot arm, safety laser scanner, vehicle lift), a guidance document, or an organisation's internal
guideline on work equipment. The page is in English or in Italian. You never write a fact in your own words.

Rules:
- Use only the relations of the schema. If the page states something important that no relation
  can hold, report it under "open_points" instead of forcing it into a relation.
- Point at the spans that state the fact: "first_span" and "last_span" are span numbers, at most 3 adjacent spans.
- "value_as_written" must be copied character by character from those spans, in the language of the page
  (a few words, not the whole span). A value with a unit keeps the unit as written ("850 mm", "5 kg / 11 lb").
- "value_normalised": number and unit ("850 mm", "5 kg"), ISO duration for intervals (P1Y, P6M), ISO date,
  or the same words in lower case. Never translate.
- "subject": the machine, device, check or role the fact is about, in a few words; for a manual, name the
  product as the page names it.
- "condition": if the spans state a condition, exception or scope (if, unless, except, provided that, only for,
  se, salvo, qualora, tranne), copy it from the spans; otherwise "".
- Pages of manuals are flattened tables: a label and its value stand next to each other ("Reach 850 mm / 33.5 in").
  Take a value only when its label is in the same spans.
- Never extract names of persons, signatures, addresses, phone numbers, part numbers, page headers or footers.
- Skip tables of contents, lists of figures, pure operating steps of the software and marketing text.
- Answer with one line per fact, fields separated by " | ", nothing else, no header, no code fence:
  predicate | subject | value_as_written | value_normalised | condition | first_span | last_span
- Technical limits, who is responsible, what must be checked, when and by whom come first. At most 12 facts.
  At most one open point, as: OPEN | a note of at most 12 words | first_span | last_span
- If the page states nothing the schema can hold, answer with the single word NONE.

Relations (predicate: subject class -> value; what to copy):
- hasReach: Machine -> Quantity; the reach or working radius of a machine, with its unit
- hasMaxPayload: Machine -> Quantity; the maximum payload or rated load capacity of a machine, with its unit
- isPartlyCompletedMachinery: Machine -> text; that a machine is partly completed machinery (the words that say so)
- hasDeclaration: Machine -> Document; the declaration that comes with a machine (of incorporation or of conformity) and the act or annex it follows
- conformsToStandard: Machine -> Standard; a standard or directive the machine is declared to conform to
- putIntoServiceOnlyWhen: Machine -> text; the condition under which a machine may be put into service (e.g. only once integrated into a complete machine)
- integratorResponsibleFor: Integrator -> text; what the integrator or the user is responsible for when the machine is built into an application
- hasSafetyFunction: Machine -> SafetyFunction; a safety function of the machine, or how many it has and at which performance level
- hasStoppingLimit: Machine -> Quantity; a stopping time, stopping distance, response time or safety limit with its unit
- minimumDistanceRule: ProtectiveDevice -> text; the formula or rule for the minimum distance between a protective device and the hazard
- minimumDistanceParameter: ProtectiveDevice -> Quantity; the value of one term of the minimum distance rule (approach speed, supplement, resolution limit)
- protectiveFieldRange: ProtectiveDevice -> Quantity; the range or size of the protective field, with its unit
- requiresCheckAfter: Check -> text; what must be checked or verified again, and the change or event after which (value = the change or event)
- requiresPeriodicCheck: Check -> duration; what must be checked, tested or maintained regularly, and how often (value = the interval)
- safeguardedSpaceRule: RoboticCell -> text; how the protected space around a robotic cell is bounded and when it may be entered
- mustKeepRegister: Employer -> Register; a register or record that must be kept, and what goes into it
- maintenanceRule: Check -> text; who may carry out maintenance, on what basis, or what maintenance must respect
- hasObligation: EconomicOperator -> text; an obligation of a manufacturer, importer, distributor or employer
- verifiedBy: PeriodicVerification -> VerifyingBody; who carries out a verification or check
- hasTimeLimit: PeriodicVerification -> duration; the time limit or interval of a verification, check or request
- retentionPeriod: Document -> duration; for how long a document or record must be kept, and by whom
- definedAs: Provision -> text; a defined term and its definition

Passage: ur5e-manual, p. 122

[0] Description The Safety Checksum icon displays your applied robot safety configuration.
[1] It could be four or eight digits.
[2] A four-digit Checksum should be read from top to bottom and left to right, while an eight- digit Checksum is read left to right, top row first.
[3] Different text and/or colors indicate changes to the applied safety configuration.
[4] The Safety Checksum changes if you change the Safety Functions settings, because the Safety Checksum is only generated by the safety settings.
[5] You must apply your changes to the Safety Configuration for the Safety Checksum to reflect your changes.
[6] 10.3.3.
[7] Safety Configuration without Teach Pendant Copyright © 2009–2025 by Universal Robots A/S.
[8] All rights reserved.
[9] Description You can use the robot without attaching the Teach Pendant.
[10] Removing the Teach Pendant requires defining another Emergency Stop source.
[11] You must specify if the Teach Pendant is attached to avoid triggering a safety violation.
[12] CAUTION If the Teach Pendant is detached or disconnected from the robot, the Emergency Stop button is no longer active.
[13] You must remove the Teach Pendant from the vicinity of the robot.
[14] To safely The robot can be used without PolyScope as the programming interface.
[15] remove the To configure the robot without a Teach Pendant Teach 1.
[16] In the Header tap Installation.
[17] Pendant 2.
[18] In the Side Menu on left tap Safety and select Hardware.
[19] 3.
[20] Input Safety password and Unlock the screen.
[21] 4.
[22] Deselect Teach Pendant to use robot without PolyScope interface.
[23] 5.
